$comment: Generated by node contract/tools/generate.mjs. Edit contract/tools, not these files.
notes: prefixes: valid says whether the text is a LAN prefix of section 10.1; contains[i] whether addresses[i], a dotted-quad IPv4 address, is inside it. An invalid prefix contains nothing.
broadcasts: valid says whether a broadcast entry is a dotted-quad IPv4 address a client sends to.

plans: documentText is fixtures/controller-document.wake-defaults.json. here.addresses are this device's addresses as a.b.c.d/length or a.b.c.d; one that is not dotted IPv4, or is in 127/8, is ignored. helpers maps a helper to its last status read this session: ready (with actions, action id to kind, when the status listed them), asleep (noRoute or hostUnreachable), unusable (authenticationFailed, hostKeyChanged, hostKeyUnknown, interpreterMissing, agentMissing, badRequest), not-driven (no system of it approved here), unknown (not read, or any other ending); a helper missing from the map is unknown. holds are the wake holds recorded for the target.

plans: steps run in order. A direct step is {kind: direct, broadcast, ports, repeats}; a helper step is {kind: helper, machine, action, readFirst}, readFirst when the helper is unknown and is read once just before its step. Every key is present, null where it does not apply. skipped gives the reason for the direct step (no-mac, ambiguous, unplaced, elsewhere) and for each helper entry (missing, self, duplicate, asleep, unusable, no-action, held, checked in that order), and ends with {kind: helpers, reason: none} when there is no direct step and no helper at all.
readiness: pollStartsMs are the milliseconds after a send at which the readiness polls start.

prefixes.name: dotted-with-dot
prefixes.purpose: Three octets and the trailing dot editors write: the /24, and nothing that merely starts with the same characters.

prefixes.name: dotted-without-dot
prefixes.purpose: Without the dot it is the same /24, matched on the octet boundary, so 192.168.10.7 is outside it.

prefixes.name: one-octet
prefixes.purpose: One octet is a /8, matched on the octet boundary: 100.64.0.1 is not in 10.

prefixes.name: one-octet-with-dot
prefixes.purpose: One octet and a dot is the same /8.

prefixes.name: cidr-24
prefixes.purpose: A CIDR /24 holds its own 256 addresses and not its neighbours'.

prefixes.name: cidr-12
prefixes.purpose: A CIDR length that is not a multiple of eight is matched on the bit boundary.

prefixes.name: empty
prefixes.purpose: An empty prefix would match every address with "starts with". It is no prefix.

prefixes.name: leading-space
prefixes.purpose: Surrounding whitespace is not trimmed: the text is not a prefix and never matches.

prefixes.name: full-address
prefixes.purpose: A full address without a length is not a prefix: it would be a /32 to one reader and a text prefix of 192.168.1.50 to another.

prefixes.name: leading-zero
prefixes.purpose: An octet with a leading zero is octal to some parsers and decimal to others, so it is neither.

prefixes.name: octet-too-large
prefixes.purpose: An octet above 255 is no octet, so the text is no prefix and matches nothing.

prefixes.name: double-dot
prefixes.purpose: Two trailing dots are not the one optional dot.

prefixes.name: host-bits-set
prefixes.purpose: A network with host bits set names an address, not a network, and is refused rather than silently widened.

prefixes.name: length-too-short
prefixes.purpose: A CIDR length below 8 would put a device on a sixteenth of the internet.

prefixes.name: wildcard
prefixes.purpose: A wildcard is not a prefix.

prefixes.name: ipv6
prefixes.purpose: IPv6 prefixes are not part of placement.

prefixes.name: addresses-not-ipv4
prefixes.purpose: Only a dotted-quad IPv4 address is inside anything: one with an octet above 255 or a leading zero is not.

broadcasts.name: broadcast-name
broadcasts.purpose: A name is never resolved: no client sends a magic packet to whatever a resolver says.

broadcasts.name: broadcast-octet-too-large
broadcasts.purpose: An octet above 255 makes it no address at all.

broadcasts.name: broadcast-hexadecimal
broadcasts.purpose: inet_aton reads this as 10.0.0.1; this contract reads it as nothing.

broadcasts.name: broadcast-empty
broadcasts.purpose: An empty entry is skipped, never sent to.

broadcasts.name: broadcast-three-octets
broadcasts.purpose: Three octets are a prefix, not an address.

plans.name: at-home
plans.purpose: At home: the direct step to the site's broadcast on the default ports, then the helpers in order.

plans.name: at-the-office
plans.purpose: At another site: no direct step, only the helpers.

plans.name: two-sites-match-neither-is-home
plans.purpose: Two sites match and neither is the target's: nothing is effective, and the target is elsewhere either way.

plans.name: helper-asleep
plans.purpose: pi's last read found no route to it: skipped, and not offered, because pi has no wake block of its own.

plans.name: asleep-helper-offered
plans.purpose: nas is asleep and has a wake block of its own, so "wake it first" is offered: a separate press, never a cascade.

plans.name: held-command-helper
plans.purpose: A hold for tower exists: the command helper is held, the declared wol helper still runs.

plans.name: held-unread-helpers
plans.purpose: With a hold, a helper not read this session cannot be shown to be a wol action, so it is held too.

plans.name: held-at-home
plans.purpose: A hold never stops the direct step.

plans.name: directed-broadcast
plans.purpose: laptop and its site name no broadcast: the directed broadcast of the placing address, on the one port laptop names.

plans.name: limited-broadcast
plans.purpose: Without the address's prefix length there is no directed broadcast: 255.255.255.255.

plans.name: lan-prefix-only
plans.purpose: old-box names no site; its deprecated lanPrefix places it, matched on the octet boundary.

plans.name: lan-prefix-elsewhere
plans.purpose: An address outside old-box's lanPrefix: elsewhere, and with no direct step and no helpers the plan says there is nothing to try.

plans.name: current-site-resolves
plans.purpose: Two sites share the subnet; the person said flat, and flat's prefix matches, so flat is effective. studio's name broadcast is skipped.

plans.name: ambiguous
plans.purpose: The same place without the person's answer: two sites match, none is picked, and the direct step is skipped as ambiguous.

plans.name: current-site-not-corroborated
plans.purpose: The person said flat, but no address is on flat's prefix: the answer does not place a device on a network it is not on.

plans.name: site-without-prefixes
plans.purpose: cabin has no prefixes, so it is taken on the person's word; nothing placed the device on a subnet, so the limited broadcast.

plans.name: no-action-duplicate-unusable
plans.purpose: pi does not list wake-tv, the second pi entry repeats the first, and nas cannot be used: every entry is skipped, each with its reason.

plans.name: loopback-and-unknown-site-ignored
plans.purpose: A loopback address places nothing and a currentSite that names no site is ignored. Helpers not read this session are read just before their step.

plans.name: current-site-elsewhere
plans.purpose: At home by address, but the person said attic, whose prefix does not match: nothing is effective, and tower is elsewhere.

plans.name: helper-not-driven
plans.purpose: No system of pi is approved on this device, so pi is unusable.

plans.name: unread-helper-is-a-step
plans.purpose: Without a hold, a helper not read this session is a step, read once just before it.

plans.name: no-mac
plans.purpose: pi has no wake block: no magic packet can be addressed to it, whatever the network, and it has no helpers.

readiness.name: nothing-sent
readiness.purpose: A step from which no packet left waits for nothing and moves straight on.

readiness.name: after-a-send
readiness.purpose: The first poll after 5 s, then every 8 s, 12.8 s and 20 s, for as long as a poll starts within 120 s of the send.
